card.name: Hiragasy
card.tagline: Merina highland spectacle of oratory, song and acrobatic dance
card.profile: Hiragasy (hira gasy, 'Malagasy song'; also vakodrazana) is a day-long musical spectacle and competition of the Merina of Madagascar's central highlands around Antananarivo, combining music, kabary oratory, singing and dance by costumed troupes (mpihira gasy) (Wikipedia; UNESCO). A performance follows a fixed structure - a sasitehaka prelude, kabary oration, songs, acrobatic dihy dance, and a closing vakodrazana; it generally involves two troupes and lasts about one hour and thirty minutes (UNESCO ICH, Hiragasy RL/01740). Costumes borrow red tunics, epaulettes and brass instruments from European military dress.
card.insight: Hiragasy was codified in the late 18th century by Merina sovereign Andrianampoinimerina, who hired musicians to rally dyke- and rice-field builders and to draw crowds for his kabary speeches; UNESCO inscribed it in 2023 at the 18th session (18.COM) in Kasane, Botswana (UNESCO ICH, RL/01740).
